rules.name: MiFID Suitability — Periodic Suitability Reviews for Advisory and Discretionary Clients
rules.source_legislation: UK MiFID (onshored MiFID II); FCA COBS 9A; FCA Supervisory Dear CEO letter (January 2023)
rules.description: The bank must conduct and document periodic suitability reviews for all clients in ongoing advisory or discretionary portfolio management relationships. Reviews must assess whether the current investment strategy remains suitable in light of the client's updated financial situation, investment objectives, risk tolerance, and investment knowledge. Failure to conduct or document suitability reviews is a recurring FCA enforcement focus. Reviews must be triggered by material changes in client circumstances, not just time-based schedules.
approval_chain: Head of Suitability (sign-off on complex cases)
disclosure_obligations: Suitability report provided to client before each investment recommendation or change in discretionary mandate
Ex-ante costs and charges disclosure in standardised MiFID format before mandate execution
Ex-post annual costs and charges statement to client
Client informed of right to receive a fresh suitability review on request at any time
constraints: Suitability reviews must be event-triggered (material change in client circumstances) in addition to time-based (minimum annual for ongoing clients)
Suitability documentation must be retained for minimum 5 years
No investment recommendation may be made without a current and documented suitability record
Automated suitability tools must be subject to a model risk governance process under PRA SS1/23 expectations

rules.name: FCA Sustainability Disclosure Requirements (SDR) — Anti-Greenwashing and Investment Labels
rules.source_legislation: FCA SDR Policy Statement PS23/16 (effective December 2024); FCA Anti-Greenwashing Rule (effective May 2024)
rules.description: From December 2024, funds sold to UK retail investors must use one of the FCA's four sustainability labels (Sustainability Focus, Sustainability Improvers, Sustainability Impact, Sustainability Mixed Goals) if making sustainability claims, or must not use sustainability-related language in fund names or marketing. The bank must implement an SDR governance process for all funds on its wealth platform and ensure Relationship Managers and marketing materials comply with the Anti-Greenwashing Rule. Greenwashing is a named FCA enforcement priority.
disclosure_obligations: Sustainability label clearly displayed on all in-scope fund factsheets, platform pages, and client reports
Consumer-facing summary of each sustainability label meaning available in plain English on the bank's wealth platform
Annual sustainability report for labelled funds covering investment approach and outcomes
Anti-greenwashing attestation for all marketing materials referencing sustainability, ESG, or responsible investing
constraints: Only one of the four FCA-prescribed labels may be used — hybrid or self-invented labels are prohibited
Unlabelled funds may not use sustainability-related names or language in marketing
SDR labels must be reviewed annually to confirm ongoing eligibility criteria are met
MPS (Model Portfolio Services) will be brought into SDR scope from 2025 SDR Phase 2 extension

rules.name: Consumer Duty Fair Value — Wealth Management Charging and Ongoing Service
rules.source_legislation: FCA Consumer Duty (PS22/9); FCA PROD; FCA Dear CEO letter (January 2023) for wealth managers
rules.description: The bank must demonstrate that its wealth management fees and ongoing service model deliver fair value to clients in the target market. This requires a product-level fair value assessment comparing the charges paid to the service received, with evidence that ongoing service is actually delivered for ongoing charges. FCA supervisory focus in 2024–2025 is on whether clients paying adviser charges are receiving commensurate ongoing service and whether closed-book clients are receiving the service they are being charged for.
disclosure_obligations: Annual fair value assessment for all wealth management products and services published to the Board
Client-facing annual service review evidencing the service activities delivered for fees charged
Remediation plan provided to FCA on request if fair value gap identified
constraints: Ongoing adviser charges may only be levied where ongoing service is demonstrably delivered
Closed-book wealth clients must be included in fair value assessments — no exemption post-July 2024
Fee structures must be clearly disclosed and easily comparable — complex or hidden charges are a Consumer Duty breach

rules.name: FCA Advice Guidance Boundary Review — Targeted Support Regime
rules.source_legislation: FCA CP23/24 (Advice Guidance Boundary Review — targeted support proposal); FCA consultation response (expected 2025–2026)
rules.description: The FCA's proposed 'targeted support' regime would allow firms to provide more prescriptive guidance to mass-market clients about specific products without triggering full regulated advice obligations. This could democratise the wealth advice funnel significantly, blurring the boundary between D2C digital platforms and advised wealth management. The bank must assess how targeted support would affect its digital wealth proposition, the advice/guidance boundary in its mobile app, and its regulatory permission structure.
disclosure_obligations: FCA consultation response submitted setting out the bank's position on targeted support
Board paper assessing commercial and regulatory implications of the targeted support regime
Updated customer-facing disclosures distinguishing between targeted support, guidance, and regulated advice when the regime commences
constraints: Until the FCA finalises rules, the existing advice/guidance boundary under FSMA and COBS applies
Targeted support communications must be clearly distinguished from regulated advice in all customer-facing materials
Any move to offer targeted support at scale requires a review of the bank's FCA investment business permissions

rules.name: Consumer Composite Investments (CCI) Regime — Revised Product Disclosures
rules.source_legislation: HM Treasury CCI consultation; FCA Consultation Paper on CCI (successor to PRIIPs/KIDs); expected 2025–2026
rules.description: The FCA is developing a UK Consumer Composite Investments (CCI) regime to replace the PRIIPs Key Information Document (KID) for retail-facing packaged investment products, structured products, and collective investment schemes. The new regime is expected to require revised disclosure documents with clearer performance scenario presentation and more prominent risk warnings. All structured products, funds, and packaged investments on the wealth platform will need updated disclosure documents before the CCI effective date.
disclosure_obligations: CCI disclosure documents produced for all in-scope products before the CCI effective date
Updated performance scenario methodology compliant with FCA CCI rules
Client-facing documentation inventory updated to replace PRIIPs KIDs with CCI documents
constraints: CCI documents must be provided to clients before purchase — not post-sale
Performance scenarios must use the FCA-prescribed methodology and stress scenario presentation
In-scope products cannot be marketed without a compliant CCI document once the regime is in force

rules.name: Open Finance — Investment and Pension Account Data Portability
rules.source_legislation: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025; FCA Open Finance roadmap; FCA Smart Data Scheme Rules for investments (anticipated)
rules.description: The Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 extends Open Banking-style data portability to investment accounts, pensions, and ISAs through Smart Data schemes. Once FCA makes scheme rules for investment data, the bank must provide standardised APIs enabling authorised third parties (investment platforms, financial planning tools, pension dashboards) to access customer wealth account data with consent. This will materially increase competition for AUM as clients can more easily compare performance and charges across providers.
approval_chain: Head of Open Banking and Data
disclosure_obligations: Investment account data portability consent disclosed to clients at onboarding from scheme effective date
Customer-facing Smart Data consent dashboard updated to include investment data sharing
Annual Smart Data participation report covering investment data APIs
constraints: Investment data must be provided in FCA-mandated standardised format
Clients must be able to revoke investment data sharing consents via the digital channel in real time
Bank must not commercially disadvantage clients who exercise their data portability rights
